limitations: Historical synthetic/model calibration only; no new scientific adjudication or nature-level inference.

original_claim.claim: On a synthetic, purely Newtonian wide-binary population with a realistic nonuniform sky footprint (declination-dependent quality/completeness gradient, anisotropic density) and zero injected acceleration-dependent kinematics, Astrolabe's baseline selection pipeline (quality cuts, theta/s window, escape-speed PM gate) recovers a v-tilde(g_N) profile whose deviation from its own Newtonian-mock comparator stays below the predeclared threshold (abs(B_i) < 0.04 in median v-tilde) in every populated g_N bin.
original_claim.kill: Any populated bin (n >= 5 pairs) shows abs(B_i) >= 0.04 in median v-tilde, reproducibly across the seed ladder (median seed-to-seed abs(B_i) at or above threshold), under the baseline nonuniform-footprint arm (R1) at the operational max_stars=8000 cap.
original_claim.evidence: ORB-11222's cataloged frozen run at Orrery 28dd5c72: R1-baseline has no reproducible primary excursion, but R0 sanity fails and R2 wrap/polar do reproduce excursions. The frozen decision rule therefore leaves this unresolved; ORB-11241 owns diagnosis.

diagnostic_control.evidence: The zero-injection null itself spans B_i in [-0.0945, +0.1655] with sd 0.0418; 34.2% of null seed-bins already sit at or above the frozen 0.04 threshold, so the threshold lies inside the null floor. The reproducibility clause (|median| > 1.4826*MAD) fires on a true null 44.1% of the time at n=3 and 24.3% at n=5, and the cap comparison disagrees spuriously 16.7% of the time.
diagnostic_control.locus: decision layer cannot support a verdict either way
diagnostic_control.protocol_note: not reclassified as a pass: the frozen arms genuinely cleared the frozen threshold, and the reproducibility clause is the protocol's own, faithfully implemented. The claim is only that this decision layer cannot distinguish that result from its own null, so the arms neither support nor refute the geometry hypothesis as scored
